sections.title: 1. Scope and who the service is for

blocks.text: Kingdom Kids LLC operates Kingdom Kids. This policy applies to the Kingdom Kids website, iOS and Android apps, and supporting API. The app offers Bible stories, read-aloud features, games, and progress views for children ages 3–10, while a parent or guardian creates and manages the family account.
Read-aloud features can use a device voice or prerecorded synthetic character narration delivered from controlled media hosts. The app does not require a child to record their voice.
A child is not asked to create an account or provide an email address or password. Parents should use a nickname—not a full legal name—when creating a child profile.
Parent account and security information
Parent email address and account identifiers.
A one-way password hash; the service does not store the readable account password.
Email-verification, password-reset, and account-deletion challenge records, attempt counts, expiry times, and security lockouts.
Access and refresh tokens used to maintain a signed-in session.
Minimal child-profile information
A parent-entered display name or nickname and a chosen character/avatar.
Reading preferences such as text size and whether narration is enabled.
Learning activity tied to the profile: stories started or completed, game attempts and submitted answers, scores, stars, completed levels, badges, and the last-played time.
Daily streak dates and the device timezone offset used to calculate a local day.
Website and waitlist information
A grown-up’s email, consent time, and signup source when they ask to join the launch waitlist.

Standard technical request information—such as IP address, request time, browser type, and error or security events—may be processed by the production host, reverse proxy, or API to deliver and protect the service. API access logs include the remote address, response status and request duration. The remote address can be a hosting proxy.
Payments and subscription records

A parent who purchases access enters payment details on Square’s hosted checkout. Kingdom Kids does not ask a child for payment information and does not store a full payment-card number or card security code.
We keep the selected plan, price and currency, the accepted billing terms, checkout operation references, and Square customer, checkout-link, order, subscription, invoice and payment identifiers.
We receive and verify the form of payment, payment and card-payment status, capture times, refunds, subscription and cancellation status, and the period of access supported by a verified payment.
Square can return masked card information, such as card type and last four digits, with a payment record.
Separately authorized complimentary access has its own grant, expiry and revocation records.
Messages to our team

The website contact form sends the subject, reply email address and message to our support inbox through our email provider. Contact messages are not saved in an application contact-message database. Please do not include passwords, verification codes, payment details or a child’s personal information in a message.
Information kept on the device

Session tokens, the selected profile, preferences, first-launch state, and optional reminder settings are stored using the device’s protected storage. Reminder notifications are scheduled locally after a grown-up grants notification permission.
Some games use device motion locally for game controls. The motion readings are not sent to the Kingdom Kids API. Narration is playback or text-to-speech; the app does not record a child’s voice.

sections.title: 3. What the current product does not collect

blocks.text: The current app does not ask for or integrate:
A child’s email address, password, birth date, school, home address, or precise location.
Contacts, photos, camera, microphone, or advertising identifiers.
Third-party advertising, behavioural advertising, or third-party analytics SDKs.
If a future release changes these practices, this policy and the relevant app-store disclosures must be updated before that release is made available.
Create, verify, secure, and recover a parent account.
Keep each child profile’s content preferences and progress separate.
Evaluate game activity, award progress, and show family-facing summaries.
Calculate streaks using the profile’s local day without requesting precise location.
Deliver requested launch updates to waitlist subscribers.
Open an owned checkout, verify purchases and refunds, manage subscription cancellation, and apply access.
Deliver contact messages and reply to requests for help.
Prevent abuse, investigate errors, protect accounts, and operate the service.
Comply with applicable law and respond to valid legal requests.
Kingdom Kids does not sell or rent personal information.
Information may be disclosed only as needed to:
Service providers used to host and deliver the website, API, database, media, payments and email, as described below.
Comply with law, court orders, or valid government requests, or protect people and the service from harm.
Complete a merger, financing, acquisition, or sale of assets, subject to notice and continued protection of the information.
Render hosts the API, application database and shared rate-limit cache.
Vercel hosts the public website and forwards its supported form requests to the API.
Cloudinary delivers private story and narration media.
Resend delivers account-security, waitlist and contact email.
Square hosts parent checkout and processes payments and provider-managed subscription billing.
Contact messages are delivered to the operator’s Google Gmail inbox.

Provider-specific storage regions, retention periods, contracts and any international-transfer safeguards have not yet been fully documented in this policy. Naming a provider does not promise that all processing stays in one country.
Parent account and associated child-profile data are kept while the account remains open.

The self-service deletion flow removes the parent account, child profiles, preferences, story activity, streak history, game progress and attempts, and a waitlist entry using the same email from the active service.

Deletion requests submitted through the public page are completed only after the requester verifies control of the grown-up email address using a short-lived code. This process can be used for both verified accounts and accounts still waiting for email verification.
Waitlist-only information is kept until launch communications are complete or the grown-up asks for removal.
Email-verification, password-reset, and account-deletion challenges are short-lived and retained only as needed for account security.

Family-account deletion does not erase all financial records. Hosted checkout, payment-proof and cancellation records remain with the parent-account link removed so an unresolved payment or request to stop future billing is not lost. These records include provider identifiers, billing terms, amounts, payment and refund evidence, access dates and cancellation state.

Account deletion requests cancellation of future subscription billing. If the provider is unavailable, the cancellation request remains pending until it can be verified; deleting an account alone is not proof that provider cancellation has completed.
Contact messages sent to our inbox and copies held by email or payment providers are not automatically erased by the family-account deletion flow.

An expired security challenge can no longer authorize an action; expiry does not mean its record is immediately erased. A fixed retention period for financial records, support email, production logs and any backups has not yet been set. These records may remain after family-account deletion.

The child experience is attached to a grown-up’s verified account. A parent chooses the child-profile nickname and avatar, can review profile information and progress, and can delete the entire family account. Kingdom Kids does not use child-profile activity for advertising or build advertising profiles.
If a parent believes a child supplied information beyond what the app requests, they should delete the account or contact the privacy address below so it can be investigated and removed.

The production service is intended to require HTTPS, hash passwords with Django’s password-security system, restrict data to the authenticated parent account, throttle sensitive endpoints, and store mobile session data in protected device storage. No security control can guarantee absolute protection, so suspected incidents should be reported promptly.
Use the account-deletion page to permanently delete an account.
Turn optional notifications off in the app or device settings.
Ask to access, correct, or remove information, including a waitlist-only email.
Exercise any additional privacy rights available in the family’s country or region.
We may need to verify that a requester controls the relevant parent account or email before completing a request.

This page will show a revised date when the policy changes. Material changes affecting family data should be communicated in the app, by email, or through another appropriate notice before they take effect.
Privacy questions or requests for Kingdom Kids LLC can be sent to kingdomkidshq@gmail.com.
